metadata.notes: Extracted requirements, ACs, and BRs from RFC-PAY-007 and integrated knowledge base source IDs (FR-1, FR-3, FR-8, FR-16, NFR-4, US-1, US-10, AC-01, AC-03, AC-05, BR-01).

features.name: Payment Method Orchestrator
features.description: Single payment orchestrator supporting eight payment methods with isolated adapters, state machine, reconciliation, and gateway failover.

requirements.text: The system shall support eight payment methods (Cards, UPI, Net Banking, Wallets & Postpaid, E-Gift Vouchers, Pay Later, EMI, and Cash on Delivery) on web, Android, and iOS from one server-driven method list.

preconditions: Checkout service has created a payment intent for an order
expected_behavior: Payment page renders server-driven list of allowed methods

requirements.text: Every payment attempt shall be idempotent and reconciled daily against gateway settlement files without losing or double-charging a payment.

expected_behavior: Daily reconciliation matches attempts against gateway settlement files

requirements.text: The system shall route traffic around a failing gateway to a secondary gateway without requiring a release.

expected_behavior: Traffic shifts to secondary gateway when primary success rate drops 10 points below 24-hour average

requirements.text: The system shall enforce payment method eligibility rules based on cart type, order amount, PIN code, and buyer history.

preconditions: Cart contains items with specific listing types (Buyer Protection, Luxury, Bulk, Standard)

requirements.text: The system shall maintain a payment intent lifecycle and a payment attempt state machine with terminal states Succeeded, Failed, COD confirmed, and Auto-refunded.

expected_behavior: Late successes after intent expiration trigger automatic refunds

requirements.text: The system shall provide method-specific initiation, callback handling, and status checking via isolated adapters.

expected_behavior: UPI polls every 3s for up to 5 min
Gift vouchers support split tender up to 3 vouchers

requirements.text: The payment API shall provide endpoints for intent creation, intent retrieval, attempt initiation, attempt status checking, webhooks, and EMI plans with signature verification and idempotency enforcement.

The system shall enforce security and compliance controls including PCI DSS scoping via gateway-hosted fields, network-tokenised saved cards, data localisation in India, and HMAC signature verification for webhooks.

expected_behavior: Card data never touches servers directly
PII and payment secrets masked or securely stored

acceptance_criteria.text: Payment page displays server-driven method list containing all applicable methods for the order.
Submitting an attempt with a duplicate Idempotency-Key within 24 hours returns the original attempt rather than creating a new charge.
Traffic automatically shifts from primary gateway to secondary gateway when success rate drops 10 points below the 24-hour average.
Buyer Protection and Luxury orders hide Cash on Delivery.
Bulk orders allow all prepaid methods and hide Cash on Delivery.
If a cart mixes types, the strictest rule wins (hiding COD for Luxury/Buyer Protection/Bulk).
EMI requires order amount >= ₹3,000 and an eligible card and tenure.
Cash on Delivery is hidden for orders > ₹50,000, unserviceable PIN codes, or buyers with 2+ refused COD orders in 90 days.
Payment intent transitions through OPEN, PARTIALLY_PAID, PAID, COD_CONFIRMED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED states correctly.
A late success received after intent expiration triggers an automatic refund.
Cards adapter redirects to 3-D Secure page and supports tokenised saved cards.
UPI adapter returns intent URI or QR code, polls every 3s for up to 5 min, and treats webhook as source of truth.
Gift vouchers allow split tender with one other method and up to 3 vouchers per order.
API endpoints return correct normalise error codes and messages (PAYMENT_DECLINED, AUTH_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, METHOD_NOT_ELIGIBLE, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, PAYMENT_TIMEOUT, INTENT_EXPIRED).
Webhooks verify HMAC signatures, check IP allow-lists, and enforce a replay window of 5 minutes.

business_rules.text: COD is blocked for Buyer Protection, Luxury, Bulk items, orders over ₹50,000, unserviceable PIN codes, and buyers with 2+ refused COD orders in the last 90 days.
EMI requires order amount of at least ₹3,000 and an eligible card/tenure combination.
Payment intent expires exactly 30 minutes after creation if unpaid.
Split tender with Gift Voucher holds the voucher amount for 30 minutes; if the second attempt fails and intent expires, held voucher funds are released.
Webhook and redirect may arrive in any order; the first terminal status wins and later ones are logged only.

preconditions: Buyer has items in cart and proceeds to checkout
expected_behavior: Server orchestrates payment across 8 methods with gateway routing and failover

clarifications.question: Which specific gateways are primary and secondary for Cards, UPI, Net Banking, and EMI?
clarifications.why: Needed to test gateway routing and failover scenarios against exact gateway names.
clarifications.answer: Assumed Gateway A is primary and Gateway B is secondary.

clarifications.question: Is the ₹50,000 COD cap and ₹10,000 OTP threshold final across all product categories?
clarifications.why: Needed to verify exact boundary values for COD limits and OTP triggers.
clarifications.answer: Assumed ₹50,000 COD cap and ₹10,000 OTP threshold apply as stated in the demo values.

assumptions.text: Gateway A is configured as the primary gateway and Gateway B as the secondary gateway for routing and failover tests.
The COD limit of ₹50,000 and OTP threshold of ₹10,000 are enforced strictly as documented.
